sections.label: Statements on NRIC questions
sections.summary: Statements will address listed oral and written questions, and NRIC numbers remain personal data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Digital Development and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our Statements will address Question Nos 1 to 37 for oral answer in yesterday’s Order Paper; Question Nos 3 to 8 and 39 to 44 for written answer in yesterday’s Order Paper; Question No 52 for oral answer in today’s Order Paper, and related questions that have been filed for subsequent Sittings.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We take the public's concerns very seriously and are very sorry that the mistake has caused them much anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I want to reassure the public that NRIC numbers remain personal data.

sections.label: Algorithms derive full NRIC numbers
sections.summary: Online algorithms make it easier to work out the full NRIC number from a partial or masked one.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They did so under the impression that the full NRIC number is secret.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, as shown by Dr Tan Wu Meng in his question, there are now algorithms that can be found online, that have made it easier to work out the full NRIC number from the partial or masked NRIC number.

sections.label: ACRA Bizfile NRIC disclosure lapse
sections.summary: A lapse in coordination between agencies led to ACRA disclosing full NRIC numbers in Bizfile's People Search.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The lapse in coordination between agencies led to ACRA's misunderstanding and the disclosure of full NRIC numbers in the People Search function of its new Bizfile portal.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At no point was our intention to disclose full NRIC numbers on a wide scale.

sections.label: Advice to private sector organisations
sections.summary: Private sector organisations should stop using NRIC numbers as authentication or default passwords, and consultations will start soon.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At this stage, we would advise private sector organisations to do two things: first, private sector organisations that are using NRIC numbers as a factor of authentication or as default passwords should stop this practice as soon as possible; and second, private sector organisations that presently collect partial NRIC numbers to identify people can continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The guidelines for the private sector have not yet changed and we will only consider how they should be updated after consulting the public.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To questions by Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Sharael Taha, we aim to start consultations soon and will provide details when ready.

sections.label: NRIC card as authenticator
sections.summary: The physical NRIC card can be an authenticator, but the NRIC number should not be used as one.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The physical NRIC card can be an authenticator, but the NRIC number should not be used as an authenticator.

sections.label: Public concerns on NRIC numbers
sections.summary: NRIC numbers are personal data, collected and used only when needed, and organisations holding them have a duty of care.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We understand the public's concerns about NRIC numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It was not our intention to make the full NRIC number widely disclosed and we are not heading in that direction.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: NRIC numbers are personal data and can be collected and used only when there is a need to.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Organisations that hold your NRIC number also have a duty of care.

sections.label: Incorrect NRIC number uses
sections.summary: The incorrect uses of the NRIC number are what needs to change.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What needs to change are the incorrect uses of the NRIC number.

sections.label: Stopping NRIC authentication use
sections.summary: NRIC numbers should not be used for authentication or as passwords, and organisations and individuals can stop using them as authenticators or passwords.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, we should not use NRIC numbers for authentication or as passwords.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is better to make these changes and rectify the problem while it is still relatively contained.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Both organisations and individuals can do their part to stop using NRIC numbers as authenticators or passwords.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: By taking action as soon as possible, we can increase protection for all of us.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This will allow us to more confidently use the NRIC number as a unique identifier, whenever we need to do so. : Mr Speaker, with your permission, I will respond to any clarifications which Members may have, after Minister Indranee Rajah has also made her Statement.
